stories.title: Calling it now...see you in LA to watch the Bills play in the Super Bowl!
stories.summary:
Getting this out there before the dawn of one of the most exciting new seasons in Bills history.  New stadium, new staff, personnel upgrades, etc - lot to be excited about.



	 



	I don't do many of these, and this is maybe my boldest calling it now with SB or bust, but I fully expect to win the division, can see 12+ wins, and I think we are and should be the favorites in the AFC today. While I have a pretty good track record on these, adding in the SB trip puts me out there a little bit on this one, but its authentically how I feel.  



	 



	Obviously the disclaimer is that is barring critical injuries...but I honestly for the first time maybe ever, really feel strongly about us representing the AFC in the Super Bowl.  I am not just saying it to say it. I have been excited for the season, optimistic, etc in the past...but something feels different this year, I really think we are going to get there.



	
		Despite online Karens feeble attempts to slander the new stadium, I think its going to prove to be a massive upgrade on home field advantage from how they engineered it for noise and the fans. 
	
	
		New HC = new energy and new ideas.  But we have the valuable benefit of CONTINUITY with the offense despite the new HC.  Yes, a frist time HC has learning curves to manage, but he has experienced support around him to help with that. More importantly to me is the offense and Allen are not having to learn new terminology, new style, new systems.  
	
	
		The offense will be top 5 again, if not the top offense in the NFL. 
		
			
				I think this is the most talented offensive group Allen has ever had collectively top to bottom - OL, RB, TE, and WR rooms combined.  
			
			
				I fully acknowledge the offense could start a little bit slow, its happened in the past and we have some personnel and staff changes to adjust to with a tough early schedule.  But come playoff time, I expect this offense will be hummng and be a real problem for teams. 
			
			
				DJ Moores impact - Not only does he give Allen his best weapons since prime Diggs, but he will make the lives and jobs easier for other playmakers like Kincaid and Shakir, not to mention allow players like Keon and Palmer to play more suitable roles rather than be forced into a more featured role.  The pass attack being able to be opened up more will also only make our elite RB room be more effective.
			
			
				BIGGET CONCERN:  Kromer retiring...but at least his philosophy stays behind as his successor has been his pupil.  And I would bet he can call Kromer for help or advice at any point if needed.
			
		
	
	
		The Defense will be more aggressive:  This is the big one for me...while a lot of new faces are on the field and the staff, I think the biggest improvement will be having a defense that can finally just go make one or two more plays in the post season that has led to us coming up short so many times. 
		
			
				We do not need them to be the 85 Bears, we just need them to not be so soft on critical downs and/or drives.  In most of our playoff losses, a single additional 3rd down stop could have flipped the outcome of those games rather than allowing a scoring drive that was the difference in those games
			
			
				BIGGEST CONCERN - A lot of new faces on the D we have not seen play together yet and several young pieces expected to play significant minutes.  
			
		
	



	I think our offense is without question going to be elite, and no one needs to go out on a limb to predict that.  But its our defense that I think will be the real difference between coming up short and getting over the hump.  I think its going to be more aggressive, less predictable, and more opportunistic.  Even just a moddest improvement in the post season could be the difference of getting over the hump, and it has the potential to be more than that.  



	 



	When I look around the AFC, I don't see a real threat staring back at me that makes me question if we can beat them.  Sure, we will lose some games during the regular season, hell we might lose week 1 like the Rams just did (the NFC darlings).  But overall for the season, I think this team proves to be amongst the elite of the league and will be a real problem for people come the post season.  
	
	GO BILLS!

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #5 Noah Ostlund
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Noah Ostlund



Drafted: 2022, BUF (16th overall), 1st round, 16th pick



Position: Center, wing (shoots left)



Born: 3/11/2004 (Age: 22) Stockholm, SWE



2025-2026 stats: GP 60 G 11 A 16 PTS 27 +11, Buffalo Sabres



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 9th last year



Noah Ostlund put together a promising rookie year for the Buffalo Sabres during the 2025–26 NHL season, recording 11 goals and 27 points across 60 games. He missed time late in the year due to an upper-body injury starting around March 25, 2026, which sidelined him for several games before he returned for the playoffs. Noah was also temporarily sent down to the Rochester Americans in December not for performance, but as a procedural “numbers game” so the Sabres could carry an extra defenseman on a road trip since he didn’t require waivers. He would return soon after.



Ostlund earned praise from coach Lindy Ruff for his strong two-way play, responsible reads, and competitive board work despite a leaner physical frame. He also consistently drives play, creates high-danger chances, and makes his linemates better. All good things to hear about your first-year player. At 5’11” and 180, the staff would still like to see him fill out a bit more and add some muscle. That is one of the few complaints on Noah last season. The 22 year old sometimes looks like his Sabres’ sweater is two sizes too big.



Also a problem area is his faceoffs. Noah struggled on the dot with just a 31.9% faceoff win percentage, which restricted his usage as a full-time center.







The coaching staff loves what Ostlund can bring to the table, and so do the fans. He has a nose for the net and is highly creative offensively, with his playmaking ability standing out in particular. Ostlund possesses an excellent skill set and plenty of hockey smarts, all while handling his defensive responsibilities well. His physicality and durability should only improve as he adds more strength, allowing him to better withstand the full (and new) 84-game grind of the NHL.



This kid has a ton of potential, and the sky is truly the limit for him. If he can stay healthy and play close to a full season, he is capable of putting up 20 goals and 55 points this year. He was sorely missed after going down in the playoffs, managing a goal and an assist in his three games played. He should also see more power-play time this season, giving him another opportunity to boost his offensive numbers. To me, Noah Ostlund seems poised for a strong sophomore breakout when the puck drops this October. I don’t anticipate any second year jinxing to suddenly pop up with this fine player.

stories.title: What have you done to help the Buffalo Bills win it all this year?
stories.summary:
What have you done to help the Buffalo Bills win it all?



	Good karma and paying it forward.



	 



	Every year, my wife and I like to escape the cold New Zealand winter and head up to the warm waters in the South Pacific islands.



	We’ve visited quite a few of the islands over the years, but our go-to destination is the Cook Islands. For those who haven’t been, the Cook Islands are a group of 15 tiny islands/atolls scattered across the vast, cobalt-blue stretch of the Pacific, somewhere between Tahiti and Samoa/Tonga.



	 



	The main island, Rarotonga, has a great vibrant community, and years ago we stumbled across a burger joint there called Vili’s. Ever since, we’ve made it a point to stop in whenever we’re on Rarotonga and fill our bellies with Vili's. They make simple burgers, but damn, are they good.



	 



	A couple of months ago, I saw a post on Facebook from Vili announcing that he was opening a sports pub next door to the burger joint. He mentioned that he hoped to eventually cover the walls with sports memorabilia, and, as luck would have it, the opening was going to take place while we were there on this year’s trip.



	 



	I immediately knew this was my opportunity to spread a little Bills love around the South Pacific.



	 



	I ordered an old-school Bruce Smith jersey (Bad Things) and a small metal Buffalo Bills sign, wrapped them up, and brought them along to give to Vili for his new pub.



	 



	On our first day on the island, my wife and I hopped on our little rental scooter and headed over to Vili’s for feed.



	 



	Sure enough, there was Vili sitting in a corner booth in his brand-new pub.



	I walked over, put the wrapped gift in front of him, and told him it was for the new sports bar.



	He was ecstatic.



	 



	He couldn’t believe someone from overseas would bring him a gift like this for his pub. He told me he was going to have the jersey framed and put in a prominent spot where everyone could see it.



	 



	Before we flew off to another island, a couple weeks later, we stopped back at Vili’s to see if the jersey had made it onto the wall yet.



	It hadn’t been framed yet, but it was already hanging behind the bar. And the Bills sign? Vili had already drilled that sucker into the wall — right where everyone has to stand to pay.   Perfect!



	 



	Having moved away from upstate New York back in 1990, I know we may not have the biggest fanbase in the world.



	But I also know one thing about Bills fans:



	Bills fans travel, and they keep their eyes wide open for other Bills fans.



	 



	I get a huge kick out of thinking that someday, some random Bills fan from Buffalo — or anywhere else — is going to find themselves on this little island in the middle of the South Pacific, wander into Vili’s for a burger and a beer, and suddenly spot a Bruce Smith jersey hanging on the wall.



	Maybe they’ll wonder how the hell it got there.



	 



	That’s the whole point.



	Pay it forward.



	 



	So, with that said...



	What have the rest of you done to help the Bills win the big one this year?  😜



	 



	Let’s go, Buffalo!



	(Vili promised me to send me a photo of the jersey once it's framed, and I'll be sure to update this post when I receive it.)

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #6 Jiri Kulich
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Jiri Kulich



Drafted: 2022 First Round, #28 overall



Size: 6’1″, 185 lbs



Position: Center (shoots left)



Born: 4/14/2004 (Age: 22) Kadan, CZE



2025-2026 stats: GP12 G3 A2 PTS5, Buffalo Sabres (NHL)



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 4th



After a breakout season when he came up to the big club from Rochester and made a spot on the top line his own, Jiri Kulich pretty much lost the whole of last season after being diagnosed with a serious blood clot. He underwent a successful procedure to have the blood clot surgically removed, and then resumed light, non-contact skating in May. During locker cleanout he confirmed he expects to resume his hockey career, and is expected to be a full participant in preseason training soon. 



It’s been so long since we’ve seen the Czech forward play that in many ways he’s going to be like a new signing for the team when he returns. Let’s not forget when he finished the 24-25 campaign, he was centering the top line and had earned Lindy Ruff’s trust in that key role. 









Kulich’s ace in the hole has been his shot, and arguably it’s the second-best one-timer on the team behind only Tage Thompson. That makes him a threat to opposing defenses who have been keying in on stopping Thompson, especially on the power play. With the man advantage and Kulich on ice, opponents will have to pick which poison they want to deal with. 



He has exceptional mobility in every direction, which not only allows him to beat defenders to the outside off the rush but he also uses that with an active stick to disrupt opponents backchecking. Kulich has been called ‘smart and sneaky‘. He is Zach Benson in many ways, but a much more rounded player than our carnie and that makes Kulich an intriguing prospect on his superstar track. 



The forward’s smooth skating and puck control even under pressure are other qualities that will strengthen the Sabres top six forward corps, and pose an even bigger threat. He has a career faceoff win percentage of 44.6% so that is one area he needs to work on, but should be in line for more minutes per night after averaging 15:03 in his first two seasons with Buffalo. 









Hopefully his blood clot issue is behind him and he can return to playing like he did two springs ago. The only reason Kulich dropped from #4 to #7 is because he missed a year – I will not be surprised at all to see him at #1 when we do this again next year.

2025-2026 Stats: GP 82 G 20 A 31 PTS 51 / Playoffs GP 13 G 2 A 5 PTS 7, NHL



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 6



Jack Quinn had the best season of his young career this past season. He set career highs in games played, goals, assists, and points while skating primarily with McCloud and Zucker on the third line. Lindy Ruff liked the chemistry between those three as he largely left the combination static throughout the season. It will be interesting to see if Ruff goes back to those three as a line for continuity purposes as they reshuffle their forward lines.




Insane play from Jack Quinn and Jason Zucker 🤩#LetsGoBuffalo pic.twitter.com/M4Ullk24NB— Buffalo Sabres (@BuffaloSabres) October 23, 2025




Quinn’s 51 points made him the 6th highest scoring player on the roster, but there is still room for him to grow. While he has become more consistent, there were stretches of last season where he’d seemingly disappear. He had three separate 4 game stretches with no points in the first half of the season. He was more consistent in the second half which helped Buffalo turn their season around in route to the division title. Buffalo needs the second half Quinn to resurface as they look to replace the departed production of Alex Tuch. Quinn will likely be asked to step into a larger role which gives him the opportunity to earn a significant payday at the end of the season. He will be a restricted free agent after next season.




JACK QUINN HAS TWO!! ✌️ #StanleyCup 🇺🇸: ABC🇨🇦: @Sportsnet & @TVASports pic.twitter.com/pnYsKFrBug— NHL (@NHL) May 17, 2026




One area Quinn showed significant improvement was his work along the walls. Particularly in the first half of the season, he was consistently losing battles which led to a lack of sustained offensive pressure. In the second half, he was much stronger in board battles and it significantly improved his effectiveness. Additionally, there were concerns about how effective he would be as the physicality of the game ramped up in the playoffs. After an unremarkable start against Boston, Quinn found his footing and was one of the more noticeable Sabre forwards against Montreal.



There is a lot to like about Quinn’s game. He will likely have the opportunity to go from a quality secondary scorer to become one of the Sabres primary scorers. Buffalo will need him to take another developmental step to build off last year’s success.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #8 Radim Mrtka
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Radim Mrtka



Drafted: 2025, BUF (9th overall), 1st round, 9th pick



Position: Defense (shoots right)



Born: 6/9/2007 (Age: 19) Havlickuv Brod, CZE



2025-2026 stats: GP 43 G 1 A 33 PTS 34  Seattle Thunderbirds



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 13th last year



Here he is, folks. The highly talented but often-traded Radim Mrtka. And by “traded,” I mean by the fans, in countless fantasy deals designed to bring a big fish to Buffalo’s top-six. (or a certain goalie some want) With the Sabres’ glut of right-handed defensive prospects, Mrtka’s name has been thrown around more than any other. He may be a skilled young player, but in the eyes of some fans, he has also been deemed expendable.



That’s a little hard to square with the organization’s view of him. Buffalo selected Mrtka ninth overall in 2025, and the 6-foot-6 defenseman has already shown the combination of size, mobility, puck skills and defensive ability that made him such an intriguing pick. He put up 34 points in 43 WHL games last season and gained valuable experience with Rochester, playing 8 games at the end of the year.







Mrtka also finished as the highest-ranked defenseman prospect on this list, narrowly edging out newcomer Daxon Rudolph. (not counting established Owen Power) So what exactly is Radim? Is he one of Buffalo’s best trade assets, a tempting piece to dangle in pursuit of a big deal? Or is he the fine young defenseman they drafted, a player soon to be leading the rush up ice in Blue and Gold?



I think the answer may ultimately be either, if I am being honest. Buffalo sees Mrtka as a potential top-four defenseman, and with his rare combination of size, skating and two-way ability, it would be awfully premature to write him off as merely a trade chip. But there is no denying the value he has. Sabres’ GM Jarmo Kekäläinen seemingly offered him up at least once already (in the failed Colton Parayko trade) and may again for the right deal. There is also no denying the overabundance of right handed defenders working their way through Buffalo’s system.









Something has to give eventually. Whether Mrtka is the one who gets moved or Buffalo decides his talent is too valuable to part with, one or two of these right-handed defensemen are likely to find themselves on the move. For now, his combination of size, mobility and upside makes him a particularly fascinating piece of the puzzle.



Mrtka is expected to turn pro full-time in 2026-27, joining the Rochester Americans as he continues his development and works toward earning a future spot on the Sabres’ blue line. Buffalo’s player-development staff still views him as a potential top-four defenseman. Unless, of course, Jarmo says otherwise.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #9 Daxon Rudolph
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Daxon Rudolph



Drafted: 2026, BUF (4th overall), 1st round, 4th pick



Position: Defense (shoots right)



Born: 3/6/2008 (Age: 18) Lacombe, Alberta, CAN



2025-2026 stats: GP 68 G 28 A 50 PTS 78 +32, Prince Albert Raiders WHL



2025 T25U25 Ranking: Unranked, undrafted



Swiped from my article after day one of the 2026 draft:



Daxon Rudolph has been compaired to both Charlie McAvoy and Zach Werenski. “He’s very calm, he makes the right plays as far as his defensive details, closes well, defends hard in the middle of the ice, gets the puck going north in a hurry. And it’s his risk meter, knowing when to jump into the rush and knowing when to hold.” said Prince Albert coach Ryan McDonald. 



Very high praise for Buffalo’s top pick last June. Rudolph has a tremendous skill set and a strong hockey IQ. He is a very good two-way defenseman, capable of being both a high-end shooter and playmaker while remaining solid and smart in his own end of the ice. He may have been selected three or four picks earlier than the “draft experts” predicted, but the Buffalo Sabres got the talent they wanted.







Daxon already has excellent size for an 18-year-old, standing 6’2″ and weighing 205 pounds. He may still have a little growing left to do, and there is no doubt he will add more strength and fill out that frame as he matures.



Rudolph is committed to playing his freshman season of college hockey at the University of Denver (NCAA) this fall. Daxon has stated that his personal goal is to spend one or two seasons at the college level before making the jump to the NHL.



Whether that timeline holds remains to be seen, especially with the amount of talent already in Buffalo and a deep wave of defensive prospects pushing for future NHL opportunities. Rudolph, however, is the highest-drafted player among that group and would appear to have an inside track—provided he continues to develop well and performs at a high level in Denver.









This 2026 draft pick put up a ridiculous stat line with the Prince Albert Raiders, recording 28 goals and 50 assists for 78 points in 68 games while posting a +32 rating. His offensive talents are what immediately stand out, but he can handle business in his own end as well. He is a strong skater whose transition game is paramount to his success, combining elite puck-moving ability with the vision and skill to move the game up the ice.



Rudolph may be the newest defenseman thrown into Buffalo’s prospect mix, but he may also be one of the first to crack the Sabres’ lineup. Stay tuned.

stories.title: USMNT weekend viewing guide: We labor on
2027 NHL Mock Draft – First Round (T McGee)
stories.summary:
DBTB –



Here we go, my fellow Sabre fans…as the school year gets underway, another Draft year has come! Now, I know we’re all focused on things like the Buffalo Sabres replicating last year’s performance, or even exceeding it, and things like Connor Hellebuyck or Kirill Marchenko joining the club. No one is thinking much about the Draft at this point in time. That’s cool. 



Still, as we discovered this off-season, one never knows how things will transpire on Draft Day. I certainly never envisioned the Sabres selecting at #4 and at #20 in the first round, but…that’s exactly what happened. So I will continue to follow these young prospects, really more for my own entertainment, but also for you, DBTB, in the event you have a hankering for some junior hockey or are, like Casey Kasem before you, keeping your feet on the ground while reaching for (future) stars! 



And while I’m most certainly an amateur when it comes to player assessment and prospect development, I can assure you that I will not rank Zach Benson as the #124 best player under 23 years old in the NHL. 



Let’s get into it. Some of you will know that the Hlinka tournament got underway in early August, and while not everyone on my list saw the ice during that tournament that sort of kick-starts the Draft year, many of them did, including 6 of my Top 10, and more than half of my first round. This year’s Hlinka did not have what could be a superior Russian group as the ban remains in place for Team Russia. But we did see some fine hockey.  



One thing about the Hlinka: it remains a weird tournament as the Americans never bring their best group (the NTDP team), while the Canadians do bring the best players in that year’s class. This is reversed in the Spring, when the US brings its NTDP team to the U-18s, while the Canadians have only a portion of their group, as many are playing in the CHL playoffs with their junior team. So it’s rare we get a true “best on best” match-up during the Draft year. That said, the defending champion Americans made it all the way to the Gold Medal game, where they were spanked by a group of Canadian kids who clearly wanted to wash the bad taste of the Olympics out of their collective mouth.  



Predictably, consensus #1 Landon Dupont was fantastic, with 8pts in the tournament, while other players like Brock England, Alexis Joseph, Jaakko Wycisk, and Boston Tait looked great. The US side had Gavin Burcar come out of nowhere to dominate, while big center Gunnar Conboy and D-Man Jake Prunty had flashes of brilliance. 



The Finns beat the Slovaks in the Bronze medal game, with Slovak Tomas Selic (not to be confused with Magnum PI) looking tremendous, but the Finns, behind Lenni Kokkonen – my favorite defender in the tournament not named Landon Dupont – Luca Santala and Miska Liljeberg really stood out. Others who got scouts attention were the Swiss forwards Jonah Neuenschwander and Alessandro Dominichelli, Czech power winger Max Mares and diminutive defender Lukas Kachlir, and the Swedes pair of massive centermen Milan Sundstrom and Dorian Eklund Aspe.                                                                   



Unlike last season’s Draft, where defensemen were the best and deepest of the position groups (for only the second time in a decade, 6 D-Men went in the Top 13), this year is heavy with forwards. Potentially, this Draft could have as many 10 centers go in the Top 20 (which would make it a hugely impactful Draft), but there’s a long way to go before we get there. However, a ton of forwards are likely to go early even with the likely #1 overall pick being blueliner Landon Dupont, a Cale Makar/Quinn Hughes type of dynamic defender that is becoming more and more coveted by NHL teams.  



Other than Dupont, there may not be another D-Man selected in the Top 10. Also notable is the extremely strong class of Russian kids eligible for this Draft. Right now, massive Nazr Privalov is likely the consensus #2 overall, but he’s also under contract in Russia until 2030. That could turn off some teams.  Still, Russia could have 6 or 7 players go in Round One, which would easily be the most in years. 



Interestingly, we’re seeing the impact that the changes to the CHL-NCAA relationship are having.  Dupont has gone to the NCAA after a huge year in the WHL; a number of players in my first round are coming from European leagues to North America to play junior hockey and have already committed to playing NCAA hockey.  Such things were extremely rare as recently as a few years back, but now, players – and their ‘advisors’ – are becoming very savvy to the new rules around where, when, and how players can advance to the NCAA and then on to pro hockey.  That will only become more prevalent in the years to come. 



What about the Sabres, you might say. Isn’t this a Sabres’ site? Indeed it is. BFLO will have one of, if not THE, youngest team in the NHL next season. Their pipeline is loaded. What could they possibly need? I thought adding a big, skilled forward might be in the cards for them. There are plenty in this Draft, and while Buffalo has some skilled complimentary forwards coming up (Poltapov, Ziemer, Novotny, Helenius, Schultz) the only big forwards who might be Top 9 forwards are this past year’s Ilia Morozov (6’3) and maybe Olivers Murnieks (6’2). So I added another one to that group as well as a quick, jack-of-all-trades centerman. Both seem like good fits, and players that they can take their time with. 



As is tradition, the order of selection is NOT my prediction for the season.  I took the odds from the Wynn Sports Book in Vegas and then fed it into Tankathon, which handled the Lottery for me.  So don’t @ me because you disagree with the order! 



Here we go, and let’s go BFLO! 



ROUND ONE:



1#1: VANCOUVER:  Landon Dupont, 6’0 RHD, NCAA



1#2: NASHVILLE: Milan Sundstrom, 6’3 C, SWE



1#3: CALGARY: Brock England, 5’11 C/W, WHL



1#4: SEATTLE: Nazr Privalov, 6’4 LW, RUS



1#5: CHICAGO: Alexis Joseph, 6’5 C, QMJHL



1#6: ST LOUIS: Dima Zhilkin, 5’10 RW, OHL



1#7: WINNIPEG: Sergei Skvortsov, 6’0 RW, RUS



1#8: DETROIT: Jonah Neuenschwander, 6’5 C/W, SWISS



1#9: NY ISLANDERS: Tomas Selic, 6’3 RW, SVK



1#10: BOSTON: Andrei Pustovoy, 6’3 RW, RUS



1#11: PITTSBURGH: Vladimir Shtyrkhunov, 6’1 RHD, QMJHL



1#12: NY RANGERS: Shaeffer Gordon-Carroll, 6’1 RW, WHL



1#13: COLUMBUS: Yevgeni Yakunin, 6’4 C, RUS



1#14: PHILADELPHIA: Jaako Wycisk, 6’1 C, OHL



1#15: LA KINGS: Tim Kazda, 6’1 LW, USHL



1#16: OTTAWA: Sammy Nelson, 6’3 C, NCAA



1#17: SAN JOSE: Gavin Burcar, 6’2 RW, WHL



1#18: NEW JERSEY: Luca Santala, 6’2 C/RW, FIN 



1#19: BUFFALO: Noah Davidson, 6’3 LW, WHL



1#20: ANAHEIM: Petr Tomek, 5’10 C, CZE



1#21: UTAH: Diego Guttierez, 6’2 RHD, US NTDP



1#22: BOSTON (TORONTO): Carter Meyer, 6’1 C, US NTDP



1#23: MONTREAL: Lenni Kokkonen, 6’2 LHD, FIN



1#24: WASHINGTON: Boston Tait, 6’2 RHD, WHL



1#25: DALLAS: Jaxon Jacobsen, 5’10 C, WHL



1#26: MINNESOTA: Max Mares, 6’6 W, QMJHL



1#27: SEATTLE (TAMPA BAY): Roberts Naudins, 6’6 LW, WHL



1#28: CHICAGO (EDMONTON): Dorian Eklund-Aspe, 6’4 C, SWE



1#29: NEW JERSEY (VEGAS): Loui Karlsson, 5’10 W, SWE



1#30: CAROLINA: Douglas Johnsson, 5’10 RHD, SWE



1#31: TORONTO (COLORADO): Brock Cripps, 5’10 RHD, WHL



1#32: CHICAGO (FLORIDA):  Gunnar Conboy, 6’4 C, USHL



SABRE’S HAUL



1#19: Noah Davidson, 6’3 LW, WHL



In the 2026 Draft, the Sabres drafted a big centerman in Ilia Morozov. Now, they add a big wing (6’3 215#) who can play some center. We know Ruff loves versatility. Davidson is a tough kid with a lot of skill to go with his size. Reminds me a bit of a Matthew Knies-kind of player. He’s not an explosive skater, but he gets around the ice well and has some escapability in his game.  What sets him apart is his intelligence.  Reads the flow of the game extremely well and uses that anticipation to get to spots before others can.  Instincts are high level.  Really good head for the game.  Sees plays before they happen, locates spots where he can get open and has a nose for the puck.  



High work rate.  Battles hard for pucks on the wall, sticks his nose into crowds in front or behind the net to recover pucks and create scoring chances.  Dangerous offensive threat who has the skill level to threaten the defense with the shot or the pass.  Excellent hands, if a puck gets anywhere close he seems to vacuum it up and instantly go on the attack.  Receives the puck well; can dangle you with his hands and long reach or make difficult passes through traffic.  



Sees the ice extremely well.  Is a terror around the net.  Has the pure strength to hold off defenders, the anticipation to find and recover pucks, and the hands to make a play in tight.  Tough to stop on deflections and operating in the slot – even tougher to stop once he collects a rebound around the crease.  Keeps his hands clean.  Good in transition as well.  Fills his lane on time, can carry the puck or go to the net, although he could stand to crash the net a bit more often rather than wait to receive the puck higher in the O-zone.  



Has a lethal shot.  The puck jumps off his stick.  Can fire lasers from the top of the circles on in but has enough variety in his shot arsenal that he can fool goalies from distance.  Deadly off the rush where he can use defenders as screens and fire off some wild snapshots with a ton of velocity, not unlike Alex Tuch.  Rips shots just as well standing still as he does in motion.  Defensively, he competes hard and seems to be positionally solid and is mindful of his check even when playing off the puck.  



Could get a little more physical edge to his game.  Huge frame should get even bigger and stronger as he gets older.  Davidson played behind the Ruck Twins at Medicine Hat (shout out to Tyler Ennis!) this past season where he put up 52P in 67 games despite getting 2nd line minutes.  Looked even better in the playoffs, where he added 12P in 15 games before losing to Daxon Rudolph’s Prince Albert club.  Will eventually enroll at Boston College.  Looks to be a legit Top 6 forward prospect with size and versatility.  A nice addition to the Sabres’ pipeline. 









                 



2#19: Riley Zupfer, 6’0 C/W, USHL:   



This do-it-all forward can be a jack-of-all-trades for the Sabres prospect pool, able to play any of the 3 forward positions and change styles like a chameleon.  One night he can be an effective shutdown center, the next night a playmaking wing.  A coach’s dream.  One thing he brings, no matter what position or style he’s playing, is a high-pace, high-energy game.  Zupfer is a slick operator with the puck.  Has good wheels, decent explosion and very good top speed once he gets moving.  Has some elusiveness in his game when carrying the puck; takes smart routes to the net.  Sees the play develop at full speed, whether with the puck or without it.  Understands how to manipulate defenders with subtle fakes or by drawing them to him only to feed his open teammates for a quality chance.  



Not a big shot but has good hands that can handle bouncing pucks and difficult passes.  They are soft enough to slide sauce through traffic to his teammates or in odd-man rushes against aggressive defenders.  His goal-scoring doesn’t take a back seat to his playmaking either.  Zupfer can rifle a hard snapshot past a goalie from distance.  Has a knack for finding open spots in coverage, where he can set up for a quick, accurate one-timer.  And again, with hands plenty good enough to make some dynamic moves with the puck in transition, he’s a true dual-threat on offense.  



Defensively, his work rate is high.  Hard-nosed.  Keeps stick-on-puck when defending and positionally he hustles to close off open space.  Doesn’t slack off on the backcheck.  Makes himself available on zone exits, especially when playing center, and knows what he’s going to do before the puck comes to him.  Relies on the safe play to clear his own end.  Zupfer put up an impressive 41P in 58 games for Des Moines in the USHL as their #2 center.  Also led the team in playoff scoring at a PPG.  Due to head to the Golden Dome of Notre Dame in 27-28.  I think he could be an Andrew Copp-type of forward down the road for the Sabres, which has a lot of value.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #10: Olen Zellweger
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Olen Zellweger



Drafted: 2021 – 2nd Round (34th Overall) by Anaheim Ducks



Position: Defense



Born: September 10th, 2003 – 22 Years Old



2025-2026 Stats: GP 76 G 7 A 15 PTS 22 / Playoffs GP 3 G 1 A 1 PTS 2, NHL



2025 T25U25 Ranking: Not Ranked



The Sabres were targeting a puck moving defenseman that could fill the shoes left vacant by Bowen Byram after he was traded to Chicago before the draft. They found a near identical match from a playstyle perspective. Olen Zellweger is an incredible skater who fits the mold of an offensive, puck moving defenseman. In his first two full NHL seasons, he has a combined 14 goals and 42 points in 138 games. He has all the tools to be the kind of offensive force on the backend that Lindy Ruff loves.



As was the case with Byram, Zellweger struggles in the defensive zone. Primarily, his decision making can lead to quality scoring chances against and led to him falling out of favor at time with Joel Quenneville last season. The Sabres don’t need him to be a stout defender, but eliminating some of the glaring miscues will go a long way. He should focus on using his elite skating skills to escape the opposing forecheck and transition to offense.




This Olen Zellweger puck retrieval is just nasty.Perfectly blends a strong initial body position into an escape. pic.twitter.com/jCzo4zYKSs— Félix Sicard (@Felix_Sicard) January 28, 2024




The opportunity for him to increase his role in Buffalo is obvious. The Sabres leaned heavily on their top 4 last season and they’re looking for a consistent partner for Owen Power. Plays like this could be one reason, particularly late in games, that could land Zellweger in that coveted position:




OLEN ZELLWEGER EVENS IT UP LATE IN THE THIRD 🤯That's his first #StanleyCup Playoff goal! 🇺🇸: @espn🇨🇦: @Sportsnet & @TVASports pic.twitter.com/XQAabAoBXL— NHL (@NHL) May 13, 2026




 After the trade, Zellweger signed a three-year contract with an affordable $3 million AAV. If he shines in an increased role, that contract will be an absolute steal for its entire duration.

Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #11 Tyson Kozak
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Tyson Kozak



Drafted: 2021 Seventh Round, #193 overall



Size: 5’11”, 185 lbs



Position: Center (shoots left)



Born: 12/29/2002 (Age: 23) Souris, MB



2025-2026 stats: GP46 G2 A4 PTS6, Buffalo Sabres (NHL)



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 14th



The Buffalo Sabres unearthed a late-round gem in Tyson Kozak, and he has paid off on a limited-minutes, bottom-six role with the Sabres signing him to a three-year, $2.325 million extension on July 1, 2025.



After a season of bouncing back and forth between Rochester and Buffalo, he spent the whole season with the NHL side last year. In typical fourth line forward style, where he lacked in point production he made up for with grit and determination despite his slight stature.



As a serviceable 4th line center, he improved his faceoff percentage last season to 48.3% but saw his role usurped at the business end of the season by Sam Carrick. However, once the former Ranger got injured Kozak got back into the side and featured in six playoff games, picking up one assist and going +2 against the Bruins and Canadiens, playing 11:25 a night. 




Random NHL Draft stat:2021 7th round pick Tyson Kozak has 6 goals and 5 assists for a total of 11 points in his NHL career. That's 6 goals 5 assists and 11 points more than every player selected combined by the Vegas Golden Knights since 2021…— Andy Provin (@AndyProvin) August 26, 2026




Kozak shows promise as a bottom six center that brings an infectious work ethic and a willingness to make his mark in the trenches, a thankless role that all teams need filled. However, you have to think this is his ceiling and there’s not much else he is going to do than what he already does for the Sabres.  



The center proved he could compete at the NHL level when his number was called. He consistently finishes checks and plays with a constant motor. While his stats won’t jump out at you, he showed a willingness to battle his way in the dirty areas of the ice to make an impact. A theme can be discovered by looking through his highlights: he is always around the net. All his NHL goals are plays in front where he does his best work, and he will be in contention for the Sabres’ 13th forward most nights and a chance to play in the bottom six as needed.

stories.title: NFL Sunday Ticket 2026
stories.summary: Just curious if anyone here is renewing their Sunday Ticket from last year. Last year because I was a new customer, I only paid around $200 for the package. This year since I would be a returning customer, it's going to cost me $480 which I really have no intention of paying. My question here is to the people that are renewing that don't have Youtube TV, have you reached out to YouTube and tried to haggle with them like with Directv to see if you could get it at a cheaper rate? And if so, is YouTube biting? I currently do not have YouTube TV so unlike when I had Directv and could just simply threaten to cancel to get a discount. I can't do that with Youtube TV. I bought the subscription separately and it looks like if I decided to get YouTube TV with it, I could actually renew Sunday Ticket for $240 but that's on top of paying $54 a month for the YouTube TV subscription. Has anyone been able to get a discount on a renewal with just the Sunday Ticket subscription? And if so, what did you do to make it happen?
